label: TP
reason: Both alerts indicate real vulnerabilities. Alert 1 (java/xss): User input flows through getParameter→getTheParameter→bar→SQL→encodeForHTML() at L66-67. The 'resolved sink value' is attacker-controlled (param/user input) even though encodeForHTML appears—it only encodes errors, not the primary query path. Alert 2 (java/sql-injection): Same flow reaches sql at L61 with user-controlled data. The condition (500/42)+196=207>200 is TRUE, so bar=param always. User input reaches SQL query without sanitization. Both alerts are TP.

evidence.note: User input from getParameter flows through getTheParameter to bar, then into SQL query at L61 without sanitization; encodeForHTML at L66-67 only handles error path
